FSEC (Faculty Senate Executive Committee) Meeting Minutes Date: Wednesday October 7, 2026 - Time: 10:00 am to 12:00 Pastore Hall Room 224 - Remote option via ZOOM Find the Acronym Glossary here Action Items: Staff will work with Pres.
Preisser on the script and slides for next week’s meeting.
Pres.
Preisser will finalize the “Liaisons” draft and create accompanying slides.
Staff will update the FSEC’s project tracker based on recent progress and pending senate action.
Staff will finalize the list of joint committee assignments so it can be attached to the FS meeting agenda and, regarding the JCODL in particular, will make sure relevant committee staff are notified of new members. 1.
Call to Order - Pres.
Preisser called the meeting to order at 10:03 am.
VP Trimm and Senators Van Wyk, Daniels, and Chen were present.
Past President Travis Williams was also on hand. 2.
Minutes for approval 2.1 Minutes of the 09/30/26 FSEC meeting.
The minutes were approved as edited by the Committee. 2.2 Minutes of the 9/17/26 FS meeting - The minutes were approved for posting as edited by the Committee.
They will be docketed for action at the 10/15/26 Faculty Senate meeting. 3.

Priority Items and New Business (50 minutes) 3.1.
Meeting Prep - 10/15/26 Faculty Senate Meeting - see also microphone duties - FSEC worked through the draft agenda item by item and approved the agenda for posting.
Items discussed included following, along with: The student-led Land Acknowledgment presentations will not be shared in advance but will be archived.
Any fliers brought by the presenters for related events will be made available near the sign-in area at the meetings.
A reminder about the Brightspace purge will be added to the announcements. 3.1.1 Status of Legislation: ● Course withdrawals legislation - will be tabled to November to give the proposer time to meet with TAAC and consider/incorporate other feedback. ● Special/Standing Committees - Draft language was updated and the accompanying slides were reviewed in detail.
The item should be ready for action: CBUN should have time to review the edits before the meeting. 3.1.2 Selection of Nominating Committee - Three nominees have agreed to serve and FSEC agreed to advance the slate of members.

Nominations will be invited from the floor but with a disclaimer about putting nominees ‘on the spot’ without them having time to consider workload and other factors. 3.1.1 Forum - College Liaisons- FSEC members offered edits to the draft legislation.
Pres.
Preisser will finalize the slides before next Thursday.
A significant subject of debate was the timing of liaison selection since serving in this capacity will be an additional duty and potential liaisons may want to know their other committee duties before committing to the role.
FSEC members questioned whether standing committee chairs should be automatically precluded from serving as liaisons.
Feedback from the forum may help clarify answers to these questions.
Pres.
Preisser hopes to reserve 20 minutes for the forum (5 for presentation and 15 for feedback). 1

3.2.
Current Project Tracker and Advance Agenda Setting updates - FSEC is on target with the priorities outlined in the tracker over the summer.
After next week’s senate meeting, the active steps and completion columns will need to be updated. 3.3.
Committee Assignment Updates 3.6.1 Standing Committee Members - updates The standing committees are set except that the College of Business will need to replace a senator who resigned. 3.6.2 Joint Committees - Still a work in progress - staff has had a lot of back and forth with various nominees and it is still hoped that all assignments can be finalized on 10/15.
Needing particular attention is the JCODL, whose membership was the subject of recent legislation. 4.
Continued Items 4.1.
Graduate student-related concerns - Sen.
Daniels followed up, noting he had a productive exchange with the Graduate School Dean, who suggested a procedural fix could solve the ‘enrollment holds’ problem his students have been having without making changes to the University Manual.

In short, providing a timeline to completion for those part time students who are progressing through their programs outside the normal timeframes, would allow the Dean to proactively notify Enrollment Services so that holds are not placed.
It was suggested that this process be piloted by Sen.
Daniels’ computer science students and if the process works, it could be expanded to others.
Sen.
Trimm noted that the English Department has similarly affected students so this might be a good option for them as well.
Sens.
Trimm and Daniels are encouraged to work with their departments and the graduate school to try out the recommended procedural ‘fix.’ The matter can be brought back to FSEC’s attention when and/or if necessary. 4.2.
Curricular Practical Training (CPT) (Internship concerns follow-up from Sen.
Daniels) There had been concern that the ICE guidance memo on CPT might be interpreted and enforced in the most draconian way, and FSEC agreed in their last meeting that Sen.
Daniels would request guidance from Vice Provost for Global Initiatives Johnson.
VP Johnson noted there is a current lawsuit about this issue and she discouraged any action while the challenge plays out.

There are concerns about students in the meantime, however, as summer 2027 internship applications are often due by December.
This timeline makes it very difficult to advise and assist students in a meaningful way as they consider their training options.
FSEC agreed to table this discussion until a legal update is available from either the Vice Provost’s or the General Counsel’s office. 4.3.
Faculty Concerns submitted through the FS Webpage - No new concerns were submitted but FSEC circled back to a couple of past concerns.
Future FS agendas will include brief updates to close the loop on anonymous inquiries.
Regarding a concern about a conflict of interest in A&S, FS President Preisser noted he had communicated with the dean who is aware of the perceived conflict. 4.4.
Continued Discussion - Creation of College Liaisons - Pres.
Preisser shared a draft of the proposed language which will be shared at the 10/15 Forum.
Several suggestions were offered and additional faculty feedback will be solicited during the Forum. 4.5.
Ongoing Discussion - Creation of a Programs Subcommittee (current draft); future forum - Draft proposal language will be shared with both the CBUM and CASC, who are 2

expected to return comments. FSEC members are encouraged to comment as well. There will be time to incorporate feedback before the December Forum. 5. Updates/Ongoing Items 5.1. Updates 5.1.1 Meetings with Administrators, Committees, or Others ● APC meeting of 10/13/26 - Pres. Preisser will confirm with the BAC Chair that the committee is receiving draft policies that may be of interest to faculty. i. Other Updates - Budget; College level governance concerns, etc. FSEC briefly moved into Executive Session to wrap up discussion of a college level governance issue related to Senate oversight over curricular matters . Returning to regular session, there was a brief discussion of the announcement that the current Provost intends to leave that role next year. It is not yet known what the job description/job ad for a new Provost will look like or how that search will be run. Questions pertained to whether or not the anticipated medical school will have its own Provost, a dean under the Provost’s position as currently understood, or some other structure altogether. It is not clear when those details will be forthcoming. 6. New Business – Open for additional items not listed in the agenda. None. 7. Closing Remarks – Recap of decisions made, action items, and plans for the next meeting. Pres. Preisser noted that Saturday’s apple picking event went very well and the FSEC considered making this an annual event for the faculty senate. Pres. Preisser also noted that he has secured a student worker to help the Retired Faculty Association (RFA) create a website that can be linked or otherwise integrated with the faculty senate’s pages. 8. Adjournment - The meeting adjourned at 11:35 am. 3

Sen.
Van Wyk will report back on any AAUP guidance related to ESI requests by faculty.

Call to Order - Pres.

Minutes for approval 2.1 Minutes of the 10/07/26 FSEC meeting.
The minutes were approved as edited by the Committee. 3.
Priority Items and New Business 3.1 Meeting Prep - 10/15/26 Faculty Senate Meeting - FSEC worked through the agenda item by item alongside the related slides and script.

A number of slide edits and additions were suggested. 3.1.1 Status of Legislation: ● Course withdrawals legislation and back-up - During and after introduction of the bill in September, feedback related to the need for clarity around required signatures, and the importance of ensuring the same withdrawal date applies to all semester-long courses was received.
It was also noted that a favorable endorsement from the TAAC, as well as CBUM, was needed.

The presentation will be short to maximize the time available for gathering feedback.
Some issues that will need to be addressed before formal proposal language advances include clarification of the timeline for selecting Liaisons.

Summer selection is problematic for 9-month faculty, and some faculty might be hesitant to volunteer before they know the full extent of their workload, including other senate committee assignments.
The actual “powers” of the committee will also need to be made clear.
The Committee should be able to offer informational reports to the senate as needed but any legislation originating with the special committee would proceed through FSEC and any other advisory committees deemed relevant. 3.1.
Current Project Tracker and Advance Agenda Setting updates - The agenda template was reviewed as updated and some reminders for the end of the year were inserted. 3.2.

FS agenda should round all the committees except that the JCODL still needs a faculty chair. 3.3.
Advance Planning for the November 19 FS meeting - including compensation forum - Tabled to next meeting. 4.
Continued Items 4.1.
Faculty Concerns submitted through the FS Webpage - No new concerns had been submitted via the anonymous form.
It was noted that reporting out anonymous concerns and the results of any FSEC inquiry or action will become a standing FS meeting agenda item.
If College Liaisons are successfully created this year, additional concerns can be addressed through them rather than through the Google form.
Pres.
Preisser noted a couple of concerns had been submitted by faculty directly to him and the issues seem to be resolved for now.
One pertained to eligible uses by the colleges of mandatory program fees.
The other was related to grant management, appropriate uses of ‘indirects’ (aka ‘f&a’ costs or institutional expenses), and whether or not certain support activities can be billed as direct grant cost incursions.
Guidance will be provided by the appropriate office. 4.2.

Ongoing Discussion - Creation of a Programs Subcommittee - VP Trimm noted draft language has gone to both CBUM and CASC for review, and actual legislation will likely not be addressed until after the Senate Forum on this topic, currently scheduled for December. 5.
Updates/Ongoing Items 5.1.
Updates 5.1.1 Meetings with Administrators, Committees, or Others Sen.
Daniels provided an update on the issue of enrollment holds affecting part time graduate students, as discussed at prior meetings.
He is actively working with the Graduate School dean to implement a “fix” which involves faculty advisors notifying the graduate school of ‘estimated time to completion’ for these students, but there is a concern about putting yet another burden on faculty.
He will keep FSEC in the loop on his progress. i.
Other Updates - Budget; College level governance concerns, etc. - Pres.
Preisser noted he and VP Trimm are meeting again with the University President and Provost in November, at which time he expects to discuss the academic calendar and the problems encountered this year with the use of Columbus Day/Indigenous Peoples Day as an instructional day.

He will also provide a preview of information that will be shared as part of the scheduled November Faculty Senate Forum on the senate service compensation model. 6.
New Business – Open for additional items not listed in the agenda. 7.1 College of Education concern: Request that when the fall semester starts late enough to require a traditional no-class day (e.g.
C/IP Day or Veteran’s Day) to be sacrificed, the Wednesday before Thanksgiving would be used instead (in part, because no support staff is available on state holidays).
Although the Administration has pushed back on this idea in the past, the alternatives 2

are not working well on the ground. FSEC agreed the idea is worth revisiting and the CoED is willing to draft a proposal for FSEC and ACC review and perhaps reintroduction to the full senate. 7. Closing Remarks – Recap of decisions made, action items, and plans for the next meeting. Sen. FSEC agreed to continue the conversation next week. 3.2.
Current Project Tracker and Advance Agenda Setting updates - Staff will update the tracker based on recent legislative activity.
The FS President will work with staff to refine draft agendas for the next couple of FS meetings. 3.3.
Committee Assignment Updates - Assignments are nearly complete, but there will be one or two more appointments pending in November. 3.4.
Advance Planning for the November 19 FS meeting - including compensation forum - The draft agenda was briefly reviewed.
The bulk of the discussion centered around the planned senate service compensation forum.
Pres.

Preisser presented slides which will be part of that presentation and discussion.
A number of suggestions were made, including reordering the slides: the graphs showing the widening margin between senate compensation rates and faculty compensation rates overall should be preceded by information on how (and how much) the senate workload has increased.
Pres.
Preisser hopes to finalize the slides soon so they can be shared with the administration as a courtesy, well before the 11/19 meeting.
FSEC members stressed that while increased compensation is a desired outcome, another goal, which should be attended to as part of the forum, would be providing clarity around the compensation model.
For example, most senators don’t seem to know which members of the leadership team are eligible for ‘stipends’ or release from normal duties as part of their Executive Committee or other Committee chair service.
Examples (anonymized) can be provided of how the various deans treat senate service and there needs to be some standardization and predictability.
In recent years, senate officers have often not been granted course release by their deans, which makes monetary compensation even more important.

It must also be made clear that compensation for service through faculty development funds (rather than funds that can be taken as pay) is not effective and this practice should be discouraged. 3.5.
Guidance for the newly formed Nominating Committee - FSEC members were asked to start thinking about senators who might make good FSEC members next year and to also consider running for the VP position.
The nominating committee would like an initial list to work from as they begin their outreach. 4.
Continued Items 4.1.
Faculty Concerns submitted through the FS Webpage - Three new concerns had been submitted.
Two were related and pertained to lack of availability of office and lab space for faculty (computer science department, in particular).
It was agreed that Pres.
Preisser will speak to the relevant Dean in hopes of finding a solution.
The third concern identified a typo in FSEC meeting minutes, which will be corrected. 4.2.
Ongoing Discussion - Creation of a Programs Subcommittee (current draft) - VP Trimm has transmitted a proposal to CBUM and CASC and will report back once he receives their feedback and reactions. 2

4.3.
College of Education concern related to using the Wednesday before Thanksgiving as a class day when needed.
The College of Education drafted a formal proposal that would include the Wednesday before Thanksgiving as a class day in exceptional circumstances in lieu of using Columbus Day/Indigenous People’s Day.
The proposal stems from the fact that the university has made an intentional effort to acknowledge the indigenous people of the area and their culture, and failing to honor the holiday detracts from that.
CoEd faculty also noted the operational and logistical problems posed by holding classes when most offices on campus are closed, making certain student-facing services unavailable.
FSEC members agreed the issue is worthy of senate consideration and approved the proposal.
It will be sent to the Calendar Committee and CBUM for review and comment. 5.
Updates/Ongoing Items 5.1.
Updates - Meetings with Administrators, Committees, or Others 5.1.1 Other Updates - Budget; College level governance concerns, etc.
FSEC members were briefed on a college-level governance issue ongoing in CHS which stands to affect curricular approval processes. 6.

New Business – Open for additional items not listed in the agenda. 7.1 UM amendments related to University College/Fannon Institute transition - Director for Academic Advising Services Cindie Cruger had submitted updates to Chapters 3 and 8 of the Manual, which are related to the transition from the old University College for Academic Success to the Fannon Institute for Student Success.
FSEC did not see anything problematic in the language at a glance, but agreed it deserved a closer read.
It will remain on next week’s agenda.
In the meantime, staff should send the draft to CBUM for review and comment, in hopes of docketing the bill on the 11/19 FS agenda. 7.2 Consideration of Posthumous Degree conferral changes (UM Chp. 8) - The Vice Provost had provided a draft of amendments to Section 8.22.50 of the UM dealing with posthumous degrees.
The amendment would allow the ‘50% completion toward degree requirements’ clause to be waived.
FSEC discussed the matter at length, weighing the importance of the so-called 50% requirement and how it could be refined and/or interpreted.

Ultimately, it was decided that, since the requirement can be waived in certain circumstances, there would seem to be no harm in removing the requirement altogether, and leaving the decision to the discretion of the department chair, dean, and university president.
Pres.
Preisser will convey the FSEC’s preferred text to theVice Provost. 7.3 Review Process for ESI Requests (esp. vis a vis AAUP contract) - Sen.
Van Wyk informed FSEC of her communication with the AAUP director who opined conclusively that ESI’s are not to be treated like annual reviews and fellow faculty should not be part of any peer review of these requests.
Any peer reviews initiated were the result of a mis-read by the chair or dean and should not be completed.
Correspondence to that effect will be sent from the AAUP to the affected department(s).
Pres.
Preisser opined that improvements to the dropdown menus in the required electronic forms could probably clear this up.

He will talk to the relevant staff and report back to the FSEC and AAUP. 7.4 The uncompensated service burden of senior faculty (LM) - This was briefly discussed at the last meeting and it was noted it would be most appropriate for the SCLC to explore the issue and make recommendations.
Sen.
Van Wyk is liaison to the SCLC and will ask that they focus some 3

effort here. Pres. Preisser stressed the importance of proposing a tangible action item or outcome for the senate. 7. Closing Remarks – Recap of decisions made, action items, and plans for the next meeting. It was noted that incidents like those in the news about Cornell University lately are troubling for everyone involved in higher education. It was wondered if there was anything preventative that the faculty can do via the faculty senate. Staff was asked to place an item on next week’s agenda for discussion/brainstorming. 8. Adjournment - The meeting adjourned at 11:45 am. 4
